title: bug: live-goal-release.test.tsx reds the whole control-room lane under suite load but passes 3/3 alone
description:
Filed by worker-bcaa6d5e from parent task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5 (Gate 3 roll-up, step 3 gate run, 2026-09-08T20:0xZ). NOT a defect of that parent — its diff is empty — and NOT a defect of any of its three children; measured to task-3697c02bf2ab41a896fcfacb125d9e46.

REPRO. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` at HEAD 8b785725:
  Test Files  1 failed | 204 passed (205)
       Tests  1 failed | 2676 passed (2677)
  FAIL src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx > the refusal path is unchanged by the fix > keeps a transport abort and a daemon refusal at different codes AND different layers
  TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="cr.release.answer"]
Reproduced 2/2 full-suite runs (23:01:05 and 23:01:53 local). The SAME file run alone passes 3/3: `cd apps/control-room && npx vitest run src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx` => `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 4 passed (4)`, three consecutive times.

DIAGNOSIS FROM THE DUMP, not inferred. The rendered DOM in the failure is the card MID-SUBMIT: the button reads `Recording your decision...` and is `disabled`, and `cr.release.base` is `disabled` — i.e. `busy === true`. `cr.release.answer` only renders once `answer !== null`, so the helper at live-goal-release.test.tsx:211 `screen.getByTestId("cr.release.answer").querySelector("code")` is a SYNCHRONOUS read taken before the submit promise has settled. Called from :284. Under an otherwise-idle machine the microtask drains before the assertion; under full-suite load it does not. Same class as gotcha-a-5s-default-timeout-flake-is-contention-not-work. Likely fix: `await screen.findByTestId("cr.release.answer")` (or wrap the click in `await act`) instead of the sync `getByTestId` — a test-only change; no evidence the production card is wrong.

OWNERSHIP MEASURED. `git log -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx` returns exactly ONE commit, 2569dd4e (task-3697c02b, "bug: a live release.decide outruns the browser's 15s transport abort"), authored 2026-09-08 21:40:21 +0300 = 18:40:21Z. The file is CLEAN at HEAD (`git status --porcelain` on it is empty), so this is landed bytes, not peer dirt. That commit is 35 minutes AFTER task-817d893f's completion 00c88cd8 (18:05:17Z, control-room `Test Files 204 passed (204)` / `Tests 2673 passed (2673)` EXIT 0), which is why the Gate 3 children's own green gates never saw it.

WHY IT ESCAPED ITS OWN ROW'S GATE: task-3697c02b's recorded verification is `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run --exclude src/live/live-runs.test.ts` => 204 files / 2621 tests EXIT 0. That run EXCLUDES a file and lands 204/2621 against the full lane's 205/2677, so it is not the lane gate its DoD stands on. Worth pinning in the fix: the gate for a control-room row is the unexcluded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

DoD SUGGESTION: make the assertion await the answer, then prove non-vacuity — the arm must still go RED when the production `answer` state is mutated to swallow the refusal code/layer distinction (rail 1: assert the code AND which layer refused, not merely that it refused), and quote an unexcluded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` count line at 205 files.
definitionOfDone: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (NO --exclude) is EXIT 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim at 205 files / 2677+ tests, run twice consecutively so a load-dependent flake cannot pass once by luck.

The repaired arm is proven non-vacuous by mutation: make the production `live-goal-release.tsx` answer path collapse the transport-abort code/layer into the daemon-refusal code/layer and confirm the arm goes RED, then restore and prove the restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup keyed on BOTH the task id and the worker id, in a call separate from the restore.

No production behaviour change is made unless a defect in `live-goal-release.tsx` is actually measured; if the fix is test-only, say so explicitly in the completion record rather than editing the component to make a test pass.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE MECHANISM AND FIND BOTH UNGUARDED READS. NO EDITS.

Read the chain and satisfy yourself the defect is structural, not probabilistic:
- goal-release.tsx:92-103 `decide()` is FIRE-AND-FORGET: `void port.submit(...).then((outcome) => { setAnswer(outcome); setBusy(false); }, ...)`. The click handler returns at once.
- live-goal-release.test.tsx:135-139 `confirmRelease()` ends with `await act(async () => { fireEvent.click(...) })`, which has no contract to await that DETACHED chain. The chain is several ticks deep — the port wrapper at live-goal-release.tsx:70-86, then `transport.sendCommand` at the test's :122 (an async fn returning another promise), plus the `refresh()` that fires the stubbed fetch.
- So the synchronous read at :211 is unguarded BY CONSTRUCTION. The DOM in the filing — button reading `Recording your decision...`, `cr.release.base` disabled — is exactly `busy === true` with `answer === null`.

NOW COUNT THE CALL SITES, because the filing names only one. `answerCode()` is called at :232, :239, :284 and :295. `:239` and `:295` each follow a `settle()` and are already covered. `:284` is the one that reds. `:232` IS THE IDENTICAL UNGUARDED SHAPE — `await confirmRelease()` at :229 then a synchronous read at :232, with only a sync `expect(wire.sends())` between them, which drains nothing. Confirm that yourself by reading; a repair aimed at :284 alone leaves an equally flaky arm eight lines above it.

REPRODUCE UNDER CONTENTION, and note this row is the opposite of every other gate on this board: it WANTS load. The arm passes 3/3 alone — measured at plan time, `cd apps/control-room && npx vitest run src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` gives `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 4 passed (4)` with the four arms at 45/10/6/13ms. So a green single-file run tells you nothing. Run the full lane, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, and if a peer is running a suite at the same time that is the ideal window, not a reason to wait. full-suite-gate was HELD by worker-409b958a at plan time (acquired 10:00:13Z, 15-minute eta). If you cannot reproduce it, say so plainly and proceed on the structural argument — do not manufacture a repro.

Both files are CLEAN landed bytes at HEAD: `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` was empty at plan time. Re-check before editing.

PROVE THE REPAIRED ARM IS NON-VACUOUS (DoD 2).

A drain that makes an assertion wait is one refactor away from a drain that makes it never look. Mutate the production surface and confirm the arm goes RED.

THE MUTATION, in the file DoD 2 names: `live-goal-release.tsx`. The port wrapper at :67-88 is where the submit result passes through on its way to `setAnswer`, and :76 (`result.ok || result.layer !== CONTROL_ROOM_TRANSPORT_LAYER`) is the seam that knows the two paths apart. Rewrite the returned result there so a transport abort carries the daemon refusal's code and layer — that is precisely the collapse DoD 2 asks for. Confirm the arm at :279 goes RED on the ASSERTION at :299-300 (`aborted` no longer differs from `refused`), NOT on a timeout: an assertion red proves the arm still reads a real answer; a timeout red would mean the drain is hiding the failure.

WHILE YOU ARE THERE, drill the fix itself: revert `answerCode` to the synchronous form and confirm the repaired arms can still be made to fail. If they stay green under contention with the sync read restored, you have not reproduced the defect and the repair is unproven — say so rather than claiming it.

RESTORE PROOF, and `git diff` alone is not it. `live-goal-release.tsx` is TRACKED and CLEAN, and the checkout is shared. Before mutating: `git status --porcelain` the exact path, copy it out of tree to `%TEMP%` under a name carrying BOTH this task id and your worker id, and record the SHA256 taken FROM THE LIVE FILE at that moment. Restore by copying the backup back. Prove it by SHA256 equality against that pre-mutation hash, in a call SEPARATE from the restore — a copy can silently no-op and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. A backup keyed only on a seat id can hold a stale vintage from an earlier session, which is why the task id is in the path.

THE LANE GATE, TWICE, UNEXCLUDED (DoD 1).

Run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — NO `--exclude` — twice consecutively, and quote the exit code and the `Test Files N passed` count line VERBATIM for each run. The unexcluded lane is the point of the clause: the row that landed this file recorded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run --exclude src/live/live-runs.test.ts` at 204 files / 2621 tests, which is not the lane its DoD stood on, and that is exactly how this defect reached the board.

THE COUNT IN DoD 1 IS A REFERENCE, NOT A LITERAL TO MATCH. It says "205 files / 2677+ tests", but epic rail 3 forbids freezing a roster count precisely because concurrent rows move these numbers. Take the PRINTED count as authoritative: a HIGHER count satisfies the clause and should be reported as such with a one-line note that a sibling row added tests. Only a LOWER file count, or any nonzero failed count, is a failure. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — a run that matched no files prints "No test files found" and exits 0.

Run at least one of the two under real contention if you can arrange it. Two green runs on a quiet host are consistent with the flake still being present; what makes them meaningful is that the drain is deterministic, so say which runs were loaded and which were quiet.

This is one package's lane and it does not need the root suite. `pnpm test` would not cover it anyway — the root vitest include has no `apps/**` — so do not quote a root count as evidence for this clause. If you also run other legs, label them; this DoD is about the control-room lane.

SAY WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY WAS, THEN THE ADVERSARIAL PASS (DoD 3).

DoD 3 is a record obligation and it is the one a rushed close gets wrong. State explicitly in the completion record that the fix is TEST-ONLY, that no defect was measured in `live-goal-release.tsx`, and that the component was touched only by the step 3 mutation drill and restored with the SHA256 proof quoted. If you DID measure a production defect, say what you measured and name it — but do not edit the component to make a test pass, which is what the clause exists to prevent.

Name both repaired call sites in the record, not just the one the filing reported. `:232` was the same unguarded shape as `:284` and a record that mentions only `:284` understates what shipped.

Put the run-by-run count lines in a row COMMENT rather than the completion summary: the summary truncates silently at 2000 characters and a severed gate table reads as a skipped gate.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: does any other arm in this file read state synchronously after an action that dispatches a detached promise — check every `getByTestId` that follows a `fireEvent`, not only the ones near `answerCode`? Does the drain change what the arm at :148 observes when it flips the read to ABORT at :163? Would the repaired arm still fail if `setAnswer` were never called at all, or does the drain make it wait forever? Is there a sibling card in `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` with the same fire-and-forget submit shape and the same synchronous read — and if so, is that a comment on this row rather than a new one, per the delivery-bias rail?

SCOPE NOTE: `isEpicFinal` is true on this row but that is an ORDER artifact. This epic's architectureNotes say it has no single integration-and-hardening row — its band parents are integration-shaped for their own bands and the whole-product proof stays on task-161b7e9d in the parent epic. Do NOT pull epic-wide regression, a docs sweep, or a whole-epic adversarial pass into this narrow test fix.

reopenReason:
DoD 1 FAILS AT QA RE-RUN. The flake is not fixed — it moved into a line this row added. Full evidence and both verbatim failure blocks: comment-8f65865377b14d1c912977db50c2dae4.

Four consecutive unexcluded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` runs at HEAD 9046ce29, quiet host, holding full-suite-gate: exit 1 / 0 / 0 / 1. Both reds are `live-goal-release.test.tsx`, both `AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1` at `expect(await sendCount(wire)).toBe(1)` — line 317 in run 1, line 289 in run 4. Both lines are this row's diff. `Received 0` means sendCount exhausted all 10 `settle()` iterations with the transport still never called.

The diagnosis in comment-ff19dac0 is right and is not what failed. The BOUND failed. `ANSWER_DRAINS = 10` is a fixed hop count at a 0ms advance; ten near-empty event-loop turns buy almost no wall clock, so under lane load they elapse before the ~3ms `crypto.subtle.digest` threadpool round trip lands. The record's own measurement says the digest outlasts 50 chained hops; the drain was set to 10.

The process-local matrix cannot catch this: its slow-* mutants lengthen the work while the drain still gets scheduled, whereas real contention starves the drain of wall clock. Four green worker runs fit a ~50% per-run rate.

`noteCode` shares that bound, so `answerCode` and `readRefusalCode` have the same insufficiency and merely did not lose in my runs. Fix it in the shared helper: bound the drain on something that actually elapses while a threadpool promise is outstanding, sized against a digest latency measured UNDER LOAD. Keep what the code got right — a missing answer must still fail fast at RTL's own error, never hang to the vitest timeout under always-on fake timers.

DoD 2 and 3 are SATISFIED; I re-verified 3, both production files are byte-identical to 2569dd4e and clean. Sibling cards, foreign flaky files and the :148 weakness stay out of scope.

NEXT ROUND: run the lane 4+ times, quote every count line including reds, make one contended.

comments.content:
THE DEFECT IS A FAMILY, NOT A FILE — findings from the adversarial pass, recorded here as a comment rather than as new rows, per the delivery-bias rail ("unrelated baseline red ... as a comment on this row — not as new rows"). A governor who wants any of this promoted can do so; I am not narrowing anything to avoid the work, and nothing below blocks this row.

=== 1. EIGHT SIBLING CARDS SHARE THE EXACT SHAPE THAT CAUSED THIS BUG ===
`grep -rn "void .*\.submit(" apps/control-room/src/v2/ --include=*.tsx` (production only):
  approvals/live-needs-you.tsx:187   void preview.submit(...).then(...)
  approvals/live-needs-you.tsx:210   void rollback.submit(...).then(...)
  goals/approve-plan.tsx:88          void approval.submit(...).then(...)
  goals/gate1-card.tsx:128           void Promise.resolve().then(() => port.submit(pending)).then(...)
  goals/gate1-v1-card.tsx:128        void port.submit(pending).then(...)
  goals/goal-deployments.tsx:157     void port.submit(...).then(...)
  goals/goal-publish.tsx:96          void port.submit(...).then(...)
  goals/goal-release.tsx:96          void port.submit(...).then(...)   <- this row's card
Every one dispatches FIRE-AND-FORGET from a click handler, and every one reaches `spendOffer`, which awaits `crypto.subtle.digest` before the transport. So in EVERY one of these cards, `await act(async () => fireEvent.click(...))` returns before the submit has been sent, and any test reading state synchronously afterwards is a load-dependent flake waiting for a busy enough lane. This is NOT a design fault in the cards — a click handler must not return a promise — it is a fault in how their tests read state.

I did not widen this row to the other seven. That would be seven files of unrelated diff on a narrow bug fix.

=== 2. FOUR OTHER CONTROL-ROOM FILES ARE ALREADY FLAKING, MEASURED ===
Observed reding the lane during this row's runs, each in a different run:
  src/v2/ops/environment-variables-screen.test.tsx   (unloaded run; passes ALONE 5/5, 36 tests)
  src/v2/goals/new-goal-prd-recovery.test.tsx        (loaded run; passes ALONE 5/5, 7 tests)
  src/doctor/doctor-console.test.tsx                 (loaded run)
  src/v2/projects/project-manager-app.test.tsx       (loaded run)
All four are CLEAN landed bytes, not peer dirt (`git status --porcelain` empty on each checked path). Each passes in isolation and reds only under lane load — the same signature as this row's defect.

ATTRIBUTION: my entire diff is ONE path, `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx`. Nothing in the repo imports a `.test.tsx`, so this diff cannot reach any of them. The (HEAD failures) minus (merge-base failures) set, intersected with my owned paths, is EMPTY. Disclosed verbatim, never hidden and never fabricated green.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BOARD: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is NOT reliably green under load today, for reasons that have nothing to do with this row. A future row whose DoD says "the control-room lane is green" should expect to meet one of these and should not attribute it to its own diff.

=== 3. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS I DID NOT FIX, STATED PLAINLY ===
The arm at :148 asserts absence four times (`expect(screen.queryByTestId("cr.release.read-refusal")).toBeNull()`). An under-drained absence assertion passes VACUOUSLY — the opposite failure mode to the one this row fixed: it cannot red spuriously, but it can go green without having observed anything. Its later positive assertions (the PR link href, the surviving typed base branch, the send count) do catch total non-advance, and the arm stayed green under every delay mutant I ran, so I judged it adequate and out of scope for a row filed about a red. Naming it so the next reader does not have to rediscover it.

=== 4. FILE SIZE ===
The test file grew 307 -> 368 lines, almost all of it the rationale comments on the three drained readers. Under the 400 hard cap; the 250 target is a PER PRODUCTION FILE rail and this is a test. I deliberately did not trim the rationale: it is what stops the next reader "simplifying" the drain back into the flake, which is exactly how this defect survived its own row's gate the first time.

Reviewed tree: HEAD 9046ce29 (the QA-session checkpoint that carries the deliverable). `git diff HEAD -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx` EMPTY, so I graded the delivered bytes, not a dirty tree. `live-goal-release.tsx` and `goal-release.tsx` are byte-identical to 2569dd4e and clean in the worktree — the step-3 drill restore is CONFIRMED independently, and DoD 3's test-only claim is TRUE.

=== FOUR CONSECUTIVE UNEXCLUDED LANE RUNS, held full-suite-gate from 11:14:52Z ===
`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (no --exclude), quiet host, nothing else of mine running:
```
run 1  exit 1   Test Files  1 failed | 204 passed (205)   Tests  1 failed | 2676 passed (2677)
run 2  exit 0   Test Files  205 passed (205)              Tests  2677 passed (2677)
run 3  exit 0   Test Files  205 passed (205)              Tests  2677 passed (2677)
run 4  exit 1   Test Files  1 failed | 204 passed (205)   Tests  1 failed | 2676 passed (2677)
```
2 of 4 RED. Both reds are `src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx`. This is not the foreign lane flake disclosed in comment-b4cb3e5c — `new-goal-prd-recovery`, `doctor-console`, `project-manager-app` and `environment-variables-screen` were all GREEN in every one of my four runs.

=== THE TWO FAILURES, VERBATIM ===
run 1:
```
FAIL src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx > the refusal path is unchanged by the fix
     > stops waiting once the daemon has ANSWERED, so a later failed read is reported again
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1 // Object.is equality
- Expected  1
+ Received  0
 ❯ src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx:317:35
    317|     expect(await sendCount(wire)).toBe(1);
```
run 4:
```
FAIL src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx > the refusal path is unchanged by the fix
     > renders a DELIVERED RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE verbatim, with its layer, and keeps it
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1 // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx:289:35
```
Line 289 and line 317 are BOTH `expect(await sendCount(wire)).toBe(1)` — both introduced by this row's diff, replacing the bare `expect(wire.sends()).toBe(1)`. `Received 0` means the drain returned with the transport still not called: `sendCount` exhausted all 10 `settle()` iterations without `wire.sends()` ever going above zero, then reported the true count, which was still 0.

=== WHY THE REPAIR IS INSUFFICIENT, not why it is wrong ===
The diagnosis in comment-ff19dac0 is CORRECT and I am not disputing it. `spendOffer` awaits `crypto.subtle.digest` before `sendCommand`, that promise resolves off Node's threadpool, and it needs REAL wall clock that no number of microtask hops can manufacture. The defect is the BOUND, not the idea. `ANSWER_DRAINS = 10` is a fixed HOP count with a 0ms advance; ten near-empty event-loop turns cost close to zero wall clock, so under a loaded lane they can all elapse before a ~3ms threadpool round trip lands. The completion record's own measurement says the digest "outlasts 50 chained hops" — the drain was then set to 10.

The 7-cell process-local mutation matrix in comment-ff19dac0 does not catch this, and that is worth understanding rather than dismissing: its `slow-*` mutants lengthen the boundary while the drain still gets scheduled against a synthetic delay the harness controls. Real contention starves the drain of wall clock instead of lengthening the work, which is the opposite direction, so the matrix stayed green. The four green worker lane runs are consistent with a ~50% per-run rate landing four heads.

=== THE SAME BOUND SITS UNDER THE OTHER TWO READERS ===
`noteCode` uses the identical `ANSWER_DRAINS = 10` with `settle()` at 0ms, so `answerCode` (:289 region, :337) and `readRefusalCode` (:320) carry the same insufficiency. They did not lose in my four runs; they are the same construction that did. A repair aimed only at `sendCount` leaves them where `answerCode` was before this row started.

I am not prescribing the fix. What the evidence says it must satisfy: the wait has to be bounded by something that ACTUALLY ELAPSES while a threadpool promise is outstanding, and its budget has to be justified against a measured digest latency UNDER LOAD rather than on an idle host. Whatever you choose, keep the property the current code got right and the record argues for well — a missing answer must still fail FAST at RTL's own error rather than hanging to the vitest timeout under this file's always-on fake timers.

=== WHAT I AM NOT ASKING FOR ===
Not the seven sibling cards in comment-b4cb3e5c finding 1. Not the four foreign flaky files in finding 2. Not the vacuous-absence weakness in finding 3. Those are correctly scoped out and the disclosure of all three is exactly right. This rejection is ONLY that this row's own file still reds the unexcluded lane.

DoD 2 and DoD 3 are SATISFIED on the evidence and I re-verified DoD 3 myself. The mutation drill, the backup keyed on both ids, the vintage grep on the backup, and the SHA256 restore in a separate call are all correct and above the bar. Only DoD 1 fails.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
ACCEPTED — drain deterministically inside the `answerCode` helper at :211 using the file's OWN `settle()`, then read synchronously. One edit at the source fixes all four call sites, needs no new import, and is deterministic rather than probabilistic: `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(0)` inside `act` exists precisely to flush the microtask queue.

REJECTED — `await screen.findByTestId("cr.release.answer")`, which the filing suggests. It is the riskier of the two and the risk is silent. This file arms fake timers in `beforeEach` for EVERY arm, and there is NO precedent in this repo for RTL's async utilities under ACTIVE fake timers: the only two control-room files that combine them (live-runs.test.tsx, prd-coverage.test.tsx) scope `vi.useFakeTimers()` inside a single `it` with `finally { vi.useRealTimers(); }`, and their `findBy`/`waitFor` arms run under REAL timers. RTL's `waitFor` polls on `setInterval`; if it does not detect vitest's fake clock it never advances, and the arm HANGS to the vitest timeout instead of failing fast — a worse failure than the flake being fixed. Not forbidden, but it must be measured before use, and `settle()` needs no such proof.

REJECTED — putting the drain inside `confirmRelease()`. It would cover the same call sites, but it also changes the timing of the arm at :148, which flips the read to ABORT at :163 in a window that opens right after `confirmRelease()` returns. Draining inside `answerCode` touches only the arms that read the answer.

REJECTED — changing the production component. `decide()` being fire-and-forget is a deliberate design (a click handler must not return a promise), and DoD 3 forbids editing the component to make a test pass absent a measured defect. No defect is measured; the fix is test-only and the completion record must say so.

REJECTED — waiting for a quiet host before the repro run. Unusually for this board, this row WANTS contention: the arm passes 3/3 alone and only reds under suite load. A peer holding full-suite-gate is the ideal repro window, not a reason to wait.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
THE FILING'S DIAGNOSIS IS RIGHT AND THE MECHANISM IS STRONGER THAN IT SAYS. `decide()` at goal-release.tsx:92-103 is FIRE-AND-FORGET: `void port.submit(...).then((outcome) => { setAnswer(outcome); setBusy(false); }, ...)`. The click handler returns immediately, so `await act(async () => { fireEvent.click(...) })` at the end of `confirmRelease()` (:138) has no contract to await that DETACHED promise chain. The synchronous read at :211 is therefore unguarded BY CONSTRUCTION, not merely usually-lucky. The chain is deep — `port.submit` wraps `wire.submit`, which reaches `transport.sendCommand` (:122, an async fn returning another promise), plus a `refresh()` that fires the stubbed `fetch` — so several ticks separate the click from `setAnswer`. The captured DOM in the filing (button reading `Recording your decision...`, `cr.release.base` disabled) is exactly `busy === true` with `answer === null`, which is that window.

TWO CALL SITES ARE UNGUARDED, NOT ONE. The filing names :284 because that is the one that lost. `:232`, in the first refusal arm, is the IDENTICAL shape — `await confirmRelease()` at :229, then a synchronous `answerCode()` at :232 with only a sync `expect(wire.sends())` between them, which drains nothing. Repairing only the :284 call site leaves an equally flaky arm in the same describe block. `:239` and `:295` each follow a `settle()` and are already covered; fixing the helper covers all four at no extra cost.

THE FILE ALREADY OWNS THE RIGHT PRIMITIVE. `settle` at :130-132 is `await act(async () => { await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms); })`. `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` flushes the microtask queue between timer ticks, which is the exact guarantee missing at :211. The arm at :252 proves it works on this component: it calls `confirmRelease()` then `await settle(5_000)` and reads state reliably.

NO PRECEDENT FOR RTL ASYNC UTILITIES UNDER ACTIVE FAKE TIMERS. `git grep -ln "findBy\|waitFor("` over apps/control-room returns 20+ files; cross-referencing against `git grep -c useFakeTimers` leaves live-runs.test.tsx and prd-coverage.test.tsx as the only overlaps, and READING both shows the overlap is illusory — live-runs.test.tsx:28-44 and prd-coverage.test.tsx:143-157 each scope fake timers inside one `it` with a `finally` restore, and their `findBy`/`waitFor` arms (live-runs :49, prd-coverage :166) are separate arms under real timers. live-goal-release.test.tsx arms fake timers in `beforeEach` at :33 for every arm in the file.

MEASURED AT PLAN TIME. The file passes alone: `cd apps/control-room && npx vitest run src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx --reporter=verbose` gives `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 4 passed (4)`, arms at 45/10/6/13ms, whole run 1.31s. `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/` is EMPTY, so both files are clean landed bytes, not peer dirt. Sizes: the test 307 lines, the component 103 — both well under the cap.

THE DoD's MUTATION SITE EXISTS IN THE FILE THE DoD NAMES. DoD 2 asks for `live-goal-release.tsx` to collapse the transport-abort code/layer into the daemon-refusal one. The port wrapper at live-goal-release.tsx:67-88 is where the submit result passes through, so rewriting the returned result's `code`/`layer` there produces exactly that collapse and lands in the named file. The distinction the arm pins comes from `spendOffer`; the wrapper's own line :76 (`result.layer !== CONTROL_ROOM_TRANSPORT_LAYER`) is the seam.

BOARD STATE: full-suite-gate is HELD by worker-409b958a, acquired 2026-09-09T10:00:13Z with a 15-minute eta and a 24-hour expiry.

`isEpicFinal: true` IS AN ORDER ARTIFACT. This epic's architectureNotes state it has no single integration-and-hardening row — its band parents are integration-shaped for their own bands and the whole-product proof stays on task-161b7e9d in the parent epic. This is a narrow test-only bug fix. Do NOT plan epic-wide regression, a docs sweep, or a whole-epic adversarial pass into it.
planningNotes.risks:
1. FIXING ONLY THE CALL SITE THE FILING NAMED. `:232` is the same unguarded shape as `:284` and will flake next. The fix belongs in the `answerCode` helper at :211, not at one call site.

2. `findByTestId` CAN HANG RATHER THAN FLAKE. Fake timers are armed for every arm in this file, and no file in this repo runs RTL async utilities under an active fake clock. If RTL's `waitFor` does not advance vitest's clock, the arm blocks to the vitest timeout — which converts a fast red into a slow one and makes the lane worse, not better.

3. THE DoD FREEZES A ROSTER COUNT, WHICH EPIC RAIL 3 FORBIDS. DoD 1 names "205 files / 2677+ tests". Concurrent rows add tests to this lane constantly. Treat the PRINTED count as authoritative: a HIGHER count satisfies the clause, and only a lower FILE count or a nonzero failed count is a failure. Quote the line verbatim either way and say which run produced it.

4. A GREEN RUN PROVES LITTLE ON A QUIET HOST. This defect is load-dependent by definition — it passed 3/3 alone at plan time and reds under the full lane. Two green lane runs are the DoD's bar, but the reasoning that makes them meaningful is that the drain is DETERMINISTIC, not that it passed twice.

5. THE DRILL TOUCHES A CLEAN TRACKED PRODUCTION FILE on a shared checkout. Back it up out of tree under a name carrying BOTH the task id and your worker id, take the SHA256 from the LIVE file before mutating, restore by copying the backup back, and prove it by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. A backup keyed only on a seat id can hold a stale vintage.

6. THE COMPONENT IS NOT THE DEFECT. `decide()` is fire-and-forget on purpose — a click handler must not return a promise. DoD 3 requires the completion record to say the fix is test-only rather than quietly editing the component.

7. full-suite-gate IS HELD. For the REPRO run that is an advantage, not a blocker: contention is the condition the defect needs.
